text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- If Finland joins EMU and the central bank switches to euro rates, Finnish Bankers' Federation says plans to start computing Helibor interest rates to make it possible for banks to keep rates linked to the current money-market reference rate.
- Very few Finns get rich by inheritance, and the biggest inheritances go to the rich and the elderly, statistics show. @
- Some MPs have hired their children as assistants and one hired her father, but most have not yet appointed aides although they got money for it this year.
- Helsinki's Jokerit wins first leg of a best-of-five round of national ice-hockey finals against Turku's Turun Palloseura (TPS).
- Finns find their families more important than jobs, and friends are more important than social esteem, survey shows.
- Finland needs special discrimination follow-up organisations to keep racism in check, seminar says. @
- Internationalisation has started to move jobs overseas with production abroad replacing exports, a study by the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) shows.
- Nokia rose to 19th position among top European companies in Price Waterhouse and Financial Times survey of 1,500 European CEOs, up seven notches. UPM-Kymmene UPM1v.HE and Kesko also in high esteem.
- Sanoma Oy's chairman Aatos Erkki is Finland's most influential media person, according to survey of advertisers and advertising agencies. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Peat energy has a future, says state-peat company managing director Esko Muhonen, adding the company also plans other forms of operations.
- State railways made a clear profit in its first 18 months as a limited company. Traffic to the east is "very profitable," says new CEO Henri Kuitunen.
- The government does not exclude reducing its stake in state telecommunications operator Telecom Finland, new minister of transport Matti Aura says. @
- National carrier Finnair in talks with travel agencies to cut their fees by two to three percent, vice president Leif Lundstrom says.
AAMULEHTI
- Police to try fining even small violations of speed limits.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Turku's advisers on the sale of local telephone operator Turun Puhelin -- valued at 427 million markka -- have requested bids from Swedish Telia, state-run Telecom Finland, the Tampere telephone operator and Finnet group and there has been some additional international interest in the company, sources say.
